newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss needs gold reserves, but not loads - SNB chief.
newsitem.headline: Swiss needs gold reserves, but not loads - SNB chief.

text.p: Switzerland needs gold reserves but not as much as it has at present, Swiss National Bank Chairman Hans Meyer was quoted as saying on Saturday.

"We need substantial gold reserves, but not an enormous amount. This would be implausible," the Blick tabloid quoted him as saying in a story about how Meyer had come up with the idea of using gold reserves to fund a planned humanitarian foundation.

The plan calls for revaluing the 2,600 tonnes of Swiss gold reserves at 60 percent of market prices and transferring seven billion Swiss francs in gold to the foundation, which would sell it over a period of some 10 years to raise money.
It would invest the proceeds in interest-bearing assets and distribute the income to victims of poverty, catastrophes, human rights abuses and the Holocaust.

The plan, which drove gold prices lower when announced this month, still needs legislative approval and the backing of Swiss voters in a referendum. Officials have said gold sales could not begin before 1999 at the earliest.
